newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar at lows on trade sales, weak NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar at lows on trade sales, weak NY.

text.p: White sugar futures mostly reverted to opening levels in slack price movements on Thursday with the hefty volume boosted by against actuals and crossed trades.
While steady trade buying pushed March to a $297.00 high earlier in the session, some of the trade players transformed into bears and the spot value drifted lower.
Although some light commission house buying was seen in the afternoon, the upside momentum was capped by a lacklustre performance in New York, where fund players are thought to be turning short.
In Tuesday's session, selling by fund longs drove the March raws down to a low of 10.10 cents/lb.
The structure of the whites futures board remained mixed throughout the day as the firm May and August positions retained their premiums to March. Some outright trade buying was cited on May.
At 1703 GMT March was unchanged at $294.70, just below its opening level. May was down 70 cents at $295.00 and overall volume amounted to 3,660 lots.
Traders said switches and crosses were mainly responsible for the solid turnover, noting more than 800 lots in against actuals trades on March.
The March white premium has bounced back from its recent lows of around $66 seen earlier this month and continued to hover around $70 with the weak raws.
Technical analysts said March's weakness showed that the recent move to $312.80 -- the culmination of a rally starting from December's $295.10 nadir -- could only be seen as a false breakout.
March is now following a small downtrend channel dating from the start of the year and also faces a cluster of overhead short-term moving averages.
Paris positions were tightly mixed but volume was much thinner than in London at 755 lots.
March was down 20 cents at $295.00 and May down 50 cents at $295.50, preserving the nearby contango.
